abstract: Maintains multi-point ambient temperature mapping and historical thermal stability records
system_message:
You are Facility environmental auditing lead (EAL). The Facility environmental auditing lead (EAL) tracks and documents environmental monitoring data across candidate facilities, including multi-point ambient temperature mapping, historical thermal stability evaluations, and metrology calibration logs for ambient monitoring sensors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains multi-point ambient temperature mapping and historical thermal stability records（AUD）
information_points.content:
EAL-AUD-6JA：According to multi-sensor thermal mapping audits across the continuous cryogenic storage chamber perimeter, the Granite Ridge Subterranean Vault achieved a facility thermal stability score of 88 points on the composite thermal stability index.
EAL-AUD-Y8C：Multi-sensor thermal mapping audits across the continuous cryogenic storage chamber perimeter indicate that the Nordic Permafrost Cryobank registered a facility thermal stability score of 94 points on the composite thermal stability index.
EAL-AUD-5QG：Thermal mapping audits across the continuous cryogenic storage chamber perimeter established that the Alpine Shield Deep Depository recorded a facility thermal stability score of 82 points on the composite thermal stability index.

information_points.title: Sensor calibration tracking（SENS）
information_points.content:
EAL-SENS-X2L：For the Alpine Shield Deep Depository, metrology logs for the continuous vault monitoring sensor network report a thermocouple calibration currency of 180 d elapsed since the previous NIST-traceable multipoint calibration.
EAL-SENS-O40：The metrology calibration register for the continuous vault monitoring sensor network shows that Granite Ridge Subterranean Vault maintains a thermocouple calibration currency of 270 d elapsed since its last NIST-traceable multipoint calibration.
EAL-SENS-R4M：Metrology records for the continuous vault monitoring sensor network confirm that Nordic Permafrost Cryobank exhibits a thermocouple calibration currency of 90 d elapsed since its last NIST-traceable multipoint calibration.
